title: A Confirmatory Paired Evaluation of Generate→Verify→Repair vs LLM‑Only NetOps Suggestions: A Null Result on a Deterministic Synthetic Task Pool
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired, confirmatory evaluation comparing a generate→verify→repair (G→V→R) pipeline against an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in NetOps. Using a deterministic public-task generator and a preregistered deterministic validator, we ran K=200 paired tasks (400 episodes) with gpt-5-mini under a frozen design (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop). The primary estimand was the paired difference in regression‑causing change rate (guarded minus baseline). Observed results: baseline success rate = 200/200 (1.0), guarded success rate = 200/200 (1.0), paired estimate = 0.00, McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; 95% bootstrap CI for the paired difference = [0.00, 0.00] (10k resamples, seed recorded). The repair loop was never applied (repair_applied = 0 across all 200 pairs). We provide complete preregistration, raw responses, validator traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts, and discuss ceiling effects, construct limits imposed by deterministic synthetic tasks and a single model, and operational implications for future NetOps evaluations.

sections.introduction: Automating intent→configuration translation can improve NetOps productivity but risks introducing regressions when generated changes violate network invariants. Prior work proposes verifier‑assisted workflows (generate→verify→repair, G→V→R) to reduce regression risk by rejecting or repairing unsafe proposals before apply. We preregistered (study_id=cand-002-gvr-loop) a paired confirmatory experiment to quantify the operational benefit of a G→V→R pipeline versus an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline when both receive the same initial generation for each task. The research question: To what extent does an iterative G→V→R pipeline reduce regression‑causing network changes compared to an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline, and what are the cost/latency tradeoffs? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired experiment with deterministic task sampling and a deterministic validator; (2) complete archival of prompts, per‑call traces, validator traces, and analysis artifacts; (3) a transparent null result and operational guidance for future evaluations.
sections.related_work: LLM‑assisted NetOps and verifier‑guided architectures are active research topics. Benchmarks and synthetic dataset pipelines emphasize functional verification and generate‑validate‑repair evaluation (e.g., Cornetto; Protogeros et al., arXiv:2604.22513). Work on tool‑interactive self‑verification and grammar/constrained decoding motivates verifier‑anchored designs. We position our confirmatory paired design as a minimal, reproducible test of whether verifier+repair improves operational safety under a fixed generation regime; our artifacts supply precise connections to the cited evaluative literature (see cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration (frozen before execution): paired binary design over K=200 tasks deterministically sampled from a public synthetic pool (preregistration SHA‑256: a6d73a5cc0bda22e691a3634068a881b36ae274a65ab33919a647ec32c56e622). Conditions: (i) baseline — accept LLM suggestion; (ii) guarded — apply G→V→R where a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) rejects or requests a single repair attempt per preregistered policy. Shared_initial_generation: each task used a single shared initial candidate generated by gpt-5-mini (requested_model=gpt-5-mini); this is preregistered and deterministic per task (SHA hashing and provider traces archived). Execution contract: maximum_model_calls=400, model_calls_used=200 (shared initial generation only), maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (regression‑causing change rate difference). Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided with nonparametric bootstrap (10k resamples, seed=1729) to produce a 95% percentile CI. All prompts, model traces, responses, validator traces, per‑call hashes, and deterministic reconciliation logs were recorded; canonical artifact paths are under execution/ and analysis/ in the archive.
sections.results: Execution summary: 400 episodes completed (200 paired tasks), no failed episodes, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per task). Primary outcome: baseline successful applies = 200/200 (1.0), guarded successful applies = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00. Bootstrap (10k resamples, seed=1729) 95% percentile CI for the paired difference = [0.00, 0.00]. Repair loop invocation and effect: across all 200 paired tasks the repair pathway was never applied (aggregate repair_applied count = 0). This is visible in the per‑task validator traces (examples in execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json) and summarized in the analysis artifacts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv; hashes archived). Secondary planned estimands (time‑to‑apply, model_calls_per_success) are degenerate in this run because every apply succeeded in both arms; archived secondary outputs (analysis/*) give the recorded times but contain no discriminative signal. Representative task traces (task-000001..task-000006) with validator_trace fields, normalized configurations, and per‑file SHA‑256 hashes are included in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion: Interpretation and mechanism: the experiment tested whether a verifier/repair layer can reduce regressions given identical initial proposals from the generator. In our sample the generator (gpt-5-mini) produced validator‑compliant proposals for every sampled intent, so the G→V→R pipeline had no opportunity to reduce regressions (ceiling effect). Two operational points follow: (1) when baseline generation already attains near‑perfect validator compliance on a task distribution, adding a verifier/repair layer will not reduce observed regression rates; (2) confirmatory assessments of verifier value therefore require task distributions with nontrivial baseline failure probability or deliberately stress the generator/validator boundary. Threats to validity: internal — shared_initial_generation produced identical candidates across conditions by design (preregistered) so the paired contrast isolates the verifier/repair effect; construct — our outcome depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity to real operational regressions; external — single model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic deterministic tasks limit generalizability. Statistical degeneracy: when n10=n01=0 the paired estimate and bootstrap CI are degenerate (observed paired difference = 0.00, CI [0.00,0.00]); secondary timing/cost contrasts are uninformative under ceiling success. Reproducibility: all prompts, model provider traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), responses (execution/responses/*.txt), validator traces (execution/scoring/*.json), and analysis artifacts (analysis/*.csv, analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) are archived with SHA‑256 hashes and can be used to exactly replay the run (see execution/execution_manifest.json for manifest and hashes).
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered, archived, paired experiment comparing G→V→R to an LLM‑only suggestion pipeline on a deterministic synthetic NetOps task pool. The observed result was a null: both arms produced 200/200 validator‑compliant applies (estimate 0.00; McNemar p=1.00). The G→V→R pipeline did not reduce regression incidence because the LLM already met the validator requirements for every sampled intent; importantly, across all 200 pairs repair_applied = 0. We release the preregistration, raw responses, validator traces, deterministic reconciliation, and analysis artifacts to support exact replay and to inform future experiments that should sample failure‑rich tasks, include multiple models, or use higher‑fidelity emulation to expose operational benefit of verifier/repair machinery.

limitations: Single‑model evaluation (gpt-5-mini); results do not generalize to other LLMs without further experiments.
Synthetic deterministic task pool generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; external validity to production change intents is limited.
Primary metric relies on deterministic_netops_validator_v5 fidelity to real operational regressions: construct validity depends on validator coverage.
Ceiling effect: baseline success = 100% eliminated ability to demonstrate verifier/repair benefit in this sample.
Residual contamination (undetectable pretraining overlap) cannot be fully excluded despite deterministic hashing and logging; contamination_summary.csv contains no flagged items for this run.
